title: The Pathetic Dragon
text: “Found her!”
At that, Keel pointed at Assistant.
“Bro! This is her! This is the girl who got snatched away by a monster!”

What?! So the girl Keel had been talking about—the one carried off by a monster—was Assistant all along? Ngh… the Rival in my head protested, “That’s why Gaelion said so, nano!” but I never imagined such a thing could actually be true.
“W-Wyndia? Wh-why are you here—”
“I—I’m the one who went and got close to that noisy village, aren’t I! It’s my fault, because I got seen on my way back.”
It seemed she’d taken shelter in Rival’s parent’s den, but had realized on her own that she was the reason we’d ended up combing the mountain in the first place.
“Hey, Motoyasu.”
Ren shot me an interrogating look, indeed.
His face all but shouted, “Nobody told me there was a kid involved in this.” Naturally, Father wore the exact same expression.
“Well, if we’d killed him, he would’ve become an enemy. Lucky thing that didn’t happen, eh, Ren?”
“Shut up. You knew about this, didn’t you?”
“Indeed I did.”

For what it was worth, Ren had heard from Father about my looping and was still half-convinced, half-doubtful. He could even use some of the enhancement methods now. He seemed to assume I’d simply scouted this all out in advance.
“Um… it seems there’s been quite the misunderstanding here… I’m, well, sorry about that.”
Father, acting as though he’d been elected spokesman, apologized to Rival’s parent.
“If you’ll stop fighting, we won’t lay a hand on you either, and we’ll see to your wounds.”
With that said, Father turned his gaze to Assistant.
“Uu…”
“It’s all right, isn’t it? You won’t fight anymore, right?”
“Right?” Father added, sliding a meaningful glance toward Rival’s parent, using Assistant as his leverage.
“Hah… very well. For that child’s sake, I shall overlook your trespass into my territory… and the way you made a mockery of me!”

That second part came out sounding awfully bitter and sharp with anger. It’s your own fault for strutting out so carelessly, I say. Do you have any idea how much trouble it was making sure you didn’t die?
“Well then… let’s pass the word along to everyone. The girl in question has been found. I’ll leave that to you.”
“Likewise. All within my territory—do not engage the intruders.”

With Father and Rival’s parent each issuing their orders, the commotion finally began to settle. And so the treatment of Rival’s parent’s wounds was completed. Assistant watched with a resentful glare at how thoroughly her father had been pummeled, but once she confirmed the wounds had healed, her face broke into a smile.
“We were super worried when you got carried off by a monster, you know.”
“None of your business.”
“It’s your fault for causing the misunderstanding.”
Assistant got scolded by both Keel and Ren for that.
“So you live in a dragon’s den?”
“Yeah. With my dad and my siblings.”
“Ohh.”

Watching Assistant and Rival’s parent together, Ren made a motion like wiping sweat from his brow, his expression relaxing with relief. I could tell he was relieved that if he hadn’t turned into an inult, he might have killed Rival’s parent and earned this girl’s eternal hatred.
“I heard this lively noise from down the mountain, so I snuck off to take a look…”

She seemed to be recounting the whole story in detail. Apparently Assistant had heard the festival bustle and gone to check it out, and while hiding to watch Keel and the others playing happily, Keel had spotted her and pulled her into the game.

“You all looked like you were having so much fun, and when everyone said they were heading home, I was going to ride back with the big brother waiting nearby, but I got spotted. I hurried home, and on the way my dad picked me up and scolded me. Then… when I heard everyone had come up the mountain, I figured Dad was going to kill you all, so I snuck out, and—”
“—found your father getting the stuffing kicked out of him by us…”
Ren looked awkward, indeed. But Assistant, your father happens to be the weakest Dragon Emperor around.
“Y-yeah. Um, well! Dad knew what was going on, so he was holding back—holding back the whole time! He’s actually way stronger than that, strong enough to wipe you all out with his breath alone!”

“Graaah!” Assistant boasted proudly about Rival’s parent, but Rival’s parent just turned his face away from the bragging. Getting pummeled into the dirt was, of course, the natural result. That’s exactly how weak he really was.
“Hmm… judging from the conversation just now… setting those two aside, the Shield Hero, is it…”

Then I noticed Rival’s parent was doing something toward Father—not just a look, but some kind of magic. Telepathic spellwork, maybe, to keep the conversation private? Incidentally, from the glance he threw, I could tell “those two” meant me and Ren. Probably still holding a grudge over getting flattened. Serves him right, I say.
“Ah… right. Huh? Um… well, yes. That girl’s an orphan, and we’ve been raising her while running a circus. Once things settle down, I intend to help rebuild her home village.”
“What should we do, I wonder?” Father said, glancing at Assistant and Keel and the others in their exchange before turning back to Rival’s parent.
“Eh? But… I understand. If that’s how it is.”
This flow of events… an unpleasant air was starting to hang over everything.
“Wyndia.”
“What is it, Dad?”
“You are the one responsible for bringing about this situation. As punishment, I hereby banish you!”
“Eh?”
Assistant stared back at Rival’s parent, utterly speechless.
“Then farewell. Never again shall you set foot in my territory. Do not think of us as parent and child any longer. In the end, you belong to the world of humans.”
“No way…”
Rival’s parent turned on his heel and began flapping his wings to head back to his den.
“Noooo! Daaaad! Don’t leave me behind!”
Rival’s parent flicked away Assistant with his tail as she clung to him desperately. Well, it was clearly all an act—the flick was calibrated just enough not to actually hurt her.
“Daaaaaaaad! No! I won’t go! I’m sorry! Please, please forgive me!”

At that heartrending wail, even I could tell Rival’s parent’s heart was being tugged at. Even though I found it somewhat unfair given how often he winds up around the village, loop after loop, I could still understand the feeling. What a pathetic Dragon Emperor, unable to keep up an act properly.

In my head, Father and the others were looking at me with complicated expressions. Oh? I felt like Ren and Itsuki from the previous loop were glaring at me too, but that must just be my imagination. I only cast a protective spell through an usaunny so you lot in this loop wouldn’t make any fatal mistakes, hop!
“Hey, no matter how you slice it, that’s way too much!”
Keel protested to Rival’s parent, standing up for Assistant who’d just been handed her banishment.
“Sure, maybe Wyndia-chan was the cause at first! But holding a grudge over getting beaten senseless is way too childish!”
At Keel’s words, Rival’s parent’s face twitched.

“Hmph. Beastman or not, you are still people of the human world who ravaged my territory. Unless I mete out fitting punishment upon Wyndia, the cause of it all, my own dignity cannot be preserved. Reckless bravado beyond one’s station only leads to a life cut short.”
“Say what you want, but you got wrecked completely!”
“Guh—”
Well, he was Rival’s parent, after all. And having already made such a spectacle of himself, he ended up getting talked down even by Keel. The one whose life nearly got cut short was you, I say.
“Whatever you say, the outcome will not change. Wyndia, return to the human world! You are forbidden from ever coming back here! GYAAAAAAAAAAAH!”
He roared, intimidating Assistant with the sound alone.
“Hiii… ah… Daaad…”

Well, since Assistant hadn’t undergone any training yet, the effect on her was bound to be strong. She let out trembling sobs, tears spilling as she curled up on the ground. Keel, on the other hand, had been raised fairly toughly by Father and the others in preparation for moments just like this, so the effect on her seemed rather thin by comparison.
